title: Saure Rahmnudeln (Sour Cream Noodles)
description: Prepared with sour cream, flour, and eggs.
steps: Let 1 schoppen of sour cream simmer in a brass pan
Stir in flour until it becomes a thick porridge and remove from heat
Beat in eggs until it becomes a firm sparrow dough
Set 1 maas of milk on the fire
Scrape noodles from the dough (laid on a sparrow board) into the boiling milk
Cover and let them cook well
Remove with a skimming spoon and let them drain well on a board
Coat a dish to be served with butter and lay the noodles crosswise over the top
Stir 2 eggs together with a little milk and sour cream, pour over the noodles and bake them beautifully golden in the oven

title: Saure Rahmstrudel (Sour Cream Strudel)
description: Prepared with sour cream, egg whites, and flour.

ingredients.name: butter the size of a walnut

steps: Put approximately 1/2 pound flour on a noodle board, add 2 egg whites, butter the size of a walnut, and a little lukewarm milk
Make a dough like for noodles but not as stiff
Work it very thoroughly for a quarter hour and let it rest for half an hour if time allows
Roll out the sheets as fine as possible and stretch the strudel on a cloth as fine as postpaper
Let it dry well
Mix 2 knife-tips of salt into thick sour cream
Beat 4 eggs into stiff snow and fold it into the cream
Place the strudel on the noodle board, coat it with cream, and roll it up
Put 1 schoppen of milk and a small piece of butter in a frying pan and let them boil together
Place the strudel in it, put the dish in an oven and let it rise

title: Schalotteis mit Schlagrahm (Shallot Ice with Whipped Cream)
description: Prepared with cream, whipped cream, and bacon.
steps: Place 1/2 pound bacon rinds with cold water on the fire and let cook for two minutes
Pour off the water, place the rinds on a clean board and scrape off the fat
Put the rinds again in a clean dish and pour 1 maas water over
Let it reduce to 3 schoppen
Strain through a hair sieve or woolen cloth and let stand for a quarter hour
Pour into a brass pan, add 6 loth sugar with a lemon rind grated into it
Add 3 schoppen thick sweet cream and let cook together as long as a hard egg
Strain through a hair sieve and let cool
Meanwhile, beat 1 schoppen whipped cream in a bowl with a white whisk or chocolate whisk until very thick
Place on a hair sieve and let drain
When the crème is cold, fold in the snow
Line a smooth deep form throughout with sugar bread so that one piece touches another, as with apple shallot
Fill the crème into it, let it set firm and turn it out onto a plate

title: Schellfisch, Gekocht (Haddock, Boiled)
description: Prepared with haddock, salt, and water.
steps: Scale the fish by laying it on a moistened board, holding it by the tail with a cloth, and using a knife held at an angle upward to remove the scales. Hold the knife at an angle so the scales do not scatter around the kitchen.
Gut the fish by cutting it open, finding the beginning and end of the intestines, loosening them with the knife, and removing all innards with your index finger.
If the interior of the fish is clean and the black skin has been removed, wash it carefully with water.
Trim the fins and tail neatly with scissors.
Place the fish on a plate, put this in the cooking pot and pour enough water over it so it is covered. For 1 l water, use 20 g salt.
Bring the prepared whole fish slowly to a boil; let whole fish come to a boil only once and then finish cooking gently.
The fish is done when the fins on the back can be pulled out easily and the flesh at the gills is white.
Remove the plate with the fish using a skimming spoon, pour off the water from the plate, wipe it clean and serve the fish with brown butter.

Mix 2 egg yolks with 1 schoppen sweet cream and pour over the mixture.
Seal the cover tightly and boil the pudding for half an hour.

For the sauce: pound 2 loth blanched almonds very fine with milk, add 1 schoppen sweet cream and 2 loth sugar grated from a lemon, bring to a boil, add 1/2 glass maraschino, and pour over the pudding.

title: Schnepfenpastete auf französische Art (Woodcock Pastry, French Style)
description: A pastry dish made with onions, berries, and bay leaves.

ingredients.name: Butter pastry dough for a 3-inch-high pastry

steps: Make a 3-inch-high pastry from butter dough
Tuck the heads of 3 cleaned woodcocks onto their breasts
Lard the woodcocks and cut them into 4 parts
Cut the breast from one woodcock
Steam the woodcocks in a casserole with a piece of butter, onions, juniper berries, bay leaves, and lemons for half an hour
Press out the woodcock intestines firmly, then mince them together with the woodcock breast, 2 shallot onions, half a lemon peel, and parsley
Remove the steamed woodcocks from the casserole
Strain the sauce through a fine sieve
Return the sauce to the casserole with the minced woodcock mixture
Cook for only 1 minute more with the juice of half a lemon, 1 glass red wine, salt, pepper, cloves, mace, and 2 tablespoons good jus
Pour half the sauce into the pastry
Lay the cooked woodcocks inside
Pour the remaining sauce over them
Cover with a butter dough lid
Brush with egg
Bake the pastry in the oven

description: A pastry dish made with goose, pork, and rusk.

ingredients.name: a handful of chopped and yellow-braised shallot onions

steps: Place 6 goose livers on a sheet of paper on a rack.
Sprinkle salt on the livers to draw out water.
Pound 3 of them as fine as a paste and cut the other 3 into small pieces, placing them in a dish.
Rub half pound pork forcemeat, 2 eggs, and 1 soaked and pressed rusk on a grater to a foam.

Add this to the pounded goose liver, half pound crushed and half pound cut truffles, 1 quint crushed mace, 1 crushed nutmeg, half loth pepper, salt, a handful of chopped and yellow-braised shallot onions, the juice from 3 lemons.
Mix everything together well and set aside.
Make a dough from half Württemberg Metze flour, three quarters pound lard, half pound butter, salt, and cold water.
Work it together firmly.
Roll out a base the thickness of a small finger and make it plate-sized.
Press the edge down firmly with the finger, keeping the dough finger-thick.
Make the pie 2 to 3 hands high.
Sprinkle 4 loth grated Parmesan cheese on the pie.
Place bacon slices and a handful of the pounded goose liver on top.
Then a layer of truffles.
Place the cut goose livers on the truffles, putting a mushroom on each piece, and continue until all is used.
Make a finger-thick lid from the butter dough.
Crimp it firmly with a pie crimper, but leave the edge 2 fingers width empty.
Make a small opening in the top of the lid and insert a plug, which remove when the pie is baked.
It is better to bake the pie the next day.
Brush it with eggs, make various flowers in the lid with the pie crimper.

description: Prepared with beer, egg yolks, and powdered sugar.
steps: In a bowl with 2 pounds flour, make a small dough with 2 spoonfuls beer yeast and warm milk
Let it rise and add 2 egg yolks, 3 loth finely powdered sugar, 1 knife point salt, and 3 tablespoons raspberry juice

Dip 4 to 6 slices at once in the wine, rub them well with the mixed spices, and place them in another dish

Let them stand covered overnight
The next day, dip and rub them again in the same way

title: Almond Tart (Amandeltaart)
description: Prepared with almonds, marmalade or jam, and butter or margarine.
steps: Soak the almonds in warm water, peel them and grind them finely.
Knead them with the butter or margarine, sugar and flour into a firm ball and divide it into two equal parts.
Press one half into a greased tart pan, making sure the layer of dough is as thin as possible. (When using a small tart pan, divide the dough into 3 parts instead.)
Bake it in a moderately warm oven until light brown and cooked through (15 to 20 minutes).
Let the cake cool, turn it out and bake the second half in the pan.
